name: Sibling Rivalry
beta: Begin where the roof band ends on its right, at a stepped section of roof, and climb any thin crack or flake to reach the roof. Clip a bolt under the roof and turn it.
overview: A so-so first pitch, then a superbly exposed bolted arete along the left edge of the slab.

current.area_walk_in: Hike a little over a mile along the Black Canyon path, then pick up a cairned track leading to the base of the rock.
current.descent: rap 80 ft to a tree, then 85 ft to the ground

name: Silver Spoon
beta: A friction slab leads into easy traversing beneath the obvious roof, ending at a perch in the gully. Four bolts and pins protect the pitch.
overview: Hugely popular beginner pitch: friction up a slab, then an easy traverse beneath the big roof to a gully stance. Its name comes from a kitchen spoon once bent onto an oak branch by the first moves.

current.descent: descend the shallow gully on foot (about 5.4 near the bottom)
current.location: on the friction slab below the prominent roof; the start once had a spoon wrapped on a scrub oak

name: Simon
beta:
The first pitch jams the right-hand crack at hand size to a comfortable terrace; the second takes a gentle, grassy crack up to a perch under the big roof, off to its right.

The third climbs a steep crack taking hands and fists on the roof's right side to a ledge shared with its companion route; the last two pitches angle up and right through broken cracks, corners and slabs. A standard rack plus a #4 cam is advised.

current.area_walk_in: Follow the Summit trail until it runs along the base of the wall, then leave it and scramble uphill in the forest until you reach the face.
current.location: right-hand crack beside the neighbouring 5.6 line

name: Simple Mind
beta: Start up on the square boulder-like block and go up and rightward on the face, clipping five bolts, to a perch with two-bolt anchors.

current.descent: rappel 11 m to the ground
current.location: starts on top of a square block east of the route Bridge of Air

name: Skid Marks
beta: Start along the west flank of the obvious arete, step onto its edge, and clip five bolts to the twin anchors at the top.
overview: An excellent, exposed arete climb high above the river, bolted to a pair of anchors.

current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)
current.location: West side of the obvious arete over the river

name: Skunk Crack
beta: Pick the leftmost of two neighbouring cracks. Bouldery moves lead into a shallow chimney and the crack beside it, after which the rock eases off to a two-bolt anchor. The start is a slippery layback up an inside corner to a flaring slot.
overview: Hard moves off the ground gain a shallow chimney, then a crack out right and easier rock up to a bolted anchor.

current.area_walk_in: The base of the formation is a short flat step from the roadside pullout; the ground at the foot is uneven.
current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)
current.location: The left-hand of two side-by-side cracks

name: Skyline Pig
beta: A steep line up a faint crack to a small stance, then finish via a prominent open corner onto the slanting south face. Bring thin to medium gear and mind the odd old pitons.
overview: Steep line up a thin, incipient crack to a small stance, then an open corner facing right that tops out on the slabby southern side.

current.area_walk_in: Walk uphill on the established trails toward the face; the long dihedral on the face makes an easy landmark to aim for.
current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)

name: Slab Happy
beta: A fine slab that curves up and rightward past four bolts. Reaching the anchors feels exposed unless you carry a big tricam.
overview: Superb curving slab line sweeping rightward over four bolts. The final moves to the anchors feel exposed without a large tricam.

current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)

name: Slippery When Dry
beta: A variation on the neighbouring route that climbs thin flakes straight up the headwall rather than traversing. The many quarter-inch bolts on the route deserve caution.
overview: The direct finish to Slippery When Wet, taking thin flakes straight up the headwall instead of traversing. Many of the bolts nearby are old quarter-inch ones, so go carefully.

current.area_walk_in: A short walk from the road to the base; the wall rises straight up on the north side.
current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)

name: Slippery When Wet
beta: Start up the easy first corner of the neighbouring route, then veer to the right across a blank slab. Small bolts and 5.9 moves carry you leftward above a roof, then traverse diagonally leftward across the 5.11a wall above, clipping five bolts, to a belay ledge. Treat the many quarter-inch bolts with care.
overview: Leaves the easy initial corner of the neighbouring dihedral route and angles right onto a blank slab. Bolts and 5.9 moves lead left over a roof, then the line traverses up left across a headwall past five bolts to a belay ledge.

current.area_walk_in: A short walk from the road to the base; the wall rises straight up on the north side.
current.descent: two-rope rappel of 135 ft, or move up right and finish at the top
current.location: starts up the easy corner of the dihedral route, then goes right onto the slab

name: Slot Machine
beta: Take the lower two pitches of a neighbouring route, then drive through the steep section toward an outrageous mantle, after which the climbing eases. Eight bolts lead to the anchor.
overview: An upper-tier bolted pitch reached via People's Choice: power up a steep face to an exciting mantel, after which the angle eases.

current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)
current.location: Starts from the belay atop the second pitch of People's Choice

name: Sorcerer
beta:
Start from a vegetated shelf under a handsome corner system that heads nearly to the top. Climb the corner at an easy grade into a recess, then move rightward on a good flake to a stance level with a roof off to the left.

The following pitch runs long with sparse protection, staying in the corner overhead and ending beneath another flake and roof.
overview: A long left-facing corner almost to the summit: an alcove and flake, a sustained layback, then a roof turned on the left.

current.area_walk_in: Follow the Lumpy Ridge trail west past the old Twin Owls area, continue beyond the Book and the Bookmark, then take a faint spur to the southeast prow. A little scrambling is needed to get to the routes on the right.
current.location: Grass ledge at the foot of the left-facing corner, roughly 30 ft right of the Labor of Lust arete

name: South Face Direct
beta:
Four pitches on steep, water-streaked slabs and grooves. The opening pitch is a steep bolted slab, and the second moves up slab with one 5.8 spot to another bolted belay.

The third is easy ground to a ledge under the big summit roof; the last pitch crosses that roof on bolts, with a few wires useful for the upper crack.
overview: A long multi-pitch climb on steep, water-polished slabs and grooves on bolts, with an optional hard bolted pitch through the summit roof.

current.descent: walk off left from the ledge below the summit roof, or head southwest down the boulder-filled gully to the road
current.detailed_rack: A few wired nuts for the crack on the top pitch

name: Climb On My Face
beta:
Delicate edging gets you to the first bolt, then enjoyable face moves drift left through two more bolts to the anchors of a neighboring route, where you can lower or rap.

To keep going, head directly above that point through two more bolts, swing rightward below an overhanging headwall and jam a crack to a comfortable belay ledge for a long pitch.
overview: Delicate edging gains the first bolt, then enjoyable face climbing continues. Parties can rap early or go on up to an overhanging headwall and a 5.9 jam crack to a good ledge; the long upper pitch is rated highly.

current.descent: rap off the neighbouring route's anchors, or walk down the ramps to the south

name: Flirty Dove
beta: Start like the roofed route beside it, but from under the roof move rightward up onto a sharply tilted slab. Edge to a bolt, follow faint cracks to the small overhang, then traverse leftward over the lip and finish in the neighboring dihedral.
overview: Edges up a steep slab to a bolt, follows faint cracks to a small overhang, then crosses leftward over the roof's top into the dihedral of a neighbouring route to finish.

current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)
current.location: starts the same as Testicle Traverse, then heads up and right after the roof, onto steep slab rock

name: Testicle Traverse
beta:
Face climb to the roof, then hand-traverse and undercling leftward under smaller roofs to reach a steep slab. A bolt protects the harder variation straight above; the alternative swings right for the easier way.

Both versions end at a stance by a horizontal crack, where you can rap or carry on up the easy slab above. Small and medium cams plus long slings help on the traverse.
overview: Excellent climbing: face moves reach the big roof, then an undercling and hand traverse leftward beneath smaller roofs reaches steeper slab rock. Clip a bolt straight up, or bear right; both ways lead to a stance on a horizontal crack.

current.descent: rap off the stance bolt and piton, or go on up the easy 5.6 slab
current.location: toward the left of the central slab, under the big roof

name: Southern Arete
beta:
The lower pitches work cracks and chimneys in a slim buttress, while the upper pitches tackle the steep headwall that caps the arete.

The line meanders, so choose whatever looks best as you go. A normal trad rack is enough, with extras sized for offwidth cracks.
overview: A huge, wandering line of roughly 25 pitches up the arete that bounds the Painted Wall on its left: cracks and chimneys on the narrow lower buttress, then a steep headwall higher up.

current.area_walk_in: Drop down the gully into the canyon, then head roughly a mile downriver along the water toward the talus fans below the wall.
current.location: The long arete bounding the Painted Wall on its left

name: Southern Comfort
beta:
Start left of a wide crack and jam a thin, tight finger crack up to a ledge inside the wide crack. Next, head up and right through a shallow leaning corner, then traverse onto knobs and into a recess in the wide crack system.

Belay on a shelf up that crack. The final pitch is easier-angle but offers no protection. The useful gear is small nuts and tiny cams.
overview: A three-pitch mix of face and crack climbing. The opening pitch jams a thin finger crack, the route then angles right through a shallow corner and across knobs, and it finishes on easier ground with little protection.

current.area_walk_in: For the south face, head west from the saddle on a brief path that leads to the cliff foot. The north face is reached separately.
current.location: just left of a wide crack

name: Plinth
beta: A friction climb up the striking slab that slants right and cuts the face. Easy ground leads to a belay platform, then bolts guide you up in one or two pitches; small gear and quickdraws are what to bring.
overview: A friction line up the slab that tilts rightward and cuts the face in two; bolts protect it and it goes in one or two pitches.

current.area_walk_in: A faint path heads into the valley toward the south, fords the stream, then climbs loose gravel to the foot of the rock. For Sphinx Crack, continue up onto the ledge along the east side.
current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)

name: Stemasaurus
beta: Easier moves past two bolts reach a big ledge, then the leaning corner above is climbed by bridging, protected by two further bolts. Nothing is fitted at the top, so lower and clean from the final bolt backed by a mid-size cam.
overview: Hard climbing to a large ledge, then a stemming problem up a leaning right-facing corner.

current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)
current.anchor: none; lower from the last bolt plus a cam

name: Stepped On
beta: Follow two cracks side by side immediately left of the arete, protected with RPs and stoppers.
overview: A short, thin stemming problem on twin cracks, often toproped.

current.area_walk_in: From the trailhead, hike west past the Twin Owls formation and follow the Black Canyon Trail to The Book, adding roughly another two-thirds of a mile beyond Twin Owls. Scramble up to the base of the Pages Wall.
current.descent: Rappel off a horn where the ramp ends westward
current.location: Twin thin cracks beside the arete, on the wall uphill and leftward of Pear Buttress's leaning flake

name: Steppenwolf
beta: A hand crack that many rate the best on the crag, finishing with face moves on top. Bring extended slings and a full 60 m rope to manage rope drag.
overview: Widely rated the best line on the crag: a hand crack that gives way to a face finish. A toprope setup needs extended slings and plenty of rope.

current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)

name: Straw Turkey
beta:
The first pitch jams a string of cracks to a belay on a diagonal crack. Next, angle leftward into an extended crack with some offwidth, then belay high at a sloping ledge.

The final pitch moves right and finishes by a mellow crack. Wires and medium cams are the rack.
overview: A three-pitch crack climb. The first pitch strings several cracks together, the second heads up and left to a lengthy crack that includes some wide moves, and the last steps right to finish in an easier crack.

current.area_walk_in: For the south face, head west from the saddle on a brief path that leads to the cliff foot. The north face is reached separately.

name: Stretch Marks
beta: Take the seam leaving the left end of the ledge, then finish via a notch to the rappel station. A rack of RPs up to a number 2 cam suits it.
overview: A thin seam and slot on a small arete near Pear Buttress.

current.descent: Single-rope rappel from an anchor where the buttress drops off
current.location: Minor arete, climbed on its right; begins off the grassy ledge's left end, a short scramble leftward from the little cave beneath Pear Buttress

name: Swinging Sirloin
beta: Deceptively tricky for how it looks: the steep face beside a ramp is climbed diagonally leftward past four bolts that carry homemade hangers, ending at twin anchors.
overview: A deceptively hard four-bolt face that trends up and left at the north end of the wall.

current.area_walk_in: A brief, steep, eroded track fords the creek and ascends the slope to the wall's foot. Numbering runs north to south; to find route one, start at the Buoux Block and head north.
current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)

name: Take the Power Back
beta: Start roughly two meters right of the previous route, follow a solid crack up and over a bulge, and continue to the same lowering anchor that route uses.

current.area_walk_in: Follow the obvious trail south from the lot, then drop around the formation through a notch and down a gully. If the ground begins to feel like fifth class, you have gone too far.
current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)
current.anchor: shared with the neighbouring route to the west
current.location: about two metres east of its western neighbour

name: Talus Food Crack
beta: A slab with some doubtful rock opens the route, with two bolts protecting its hardest moves. After that, jam a crack that widens from hands to fists, trending up and to the right.
overview: A crack system that leans rightward at the far left end of the wall, starting beneath the prominent split in the southwest face. It mixes a brief bolted slab start with sustained hand-to-fist jamming.

current.area_walk_in: A faint path heads into the valley toward the south, fords the stream, then climbs loose gravel to the foot of the rock. For Sphinx Crack, continue up onto the ledge along the east side.
current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)
current.location: far-left part of the southwest face beneath the obvious crack

name: The Damage Done
beta: Powerful moves through a steep overhang open the route, which then drifts toward the right-hand portion of the face where precise footwork takes over. Five bolts protect it.
overview: The Needle's best-known sport line: burly roof moves, then a rightward wander where precise footwork matters.

current.area_walk_in: From the signed trailhead on Peak View Drive, a trail of about three quarters of a mile climbs roughly 400 feet to the crag, usually taking 20 to 30 minutes.
current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)

name: Gear and Clothing
beta:
The first pitch goes through a slot onto a ledge, then leftward on a thin crack to a belay by a good horn. Next come a crack and a right-facing dihedral, a roof and a chimney, to a bivy-friendly shelf on the left.

After that a large ramp trends right to a thin crack leading up to a hanging belay anchored by two bolts below a big roof.
overview: A big-wall aid line that climbs the Green Pillar and then continues straight up the headwall beside La Dolce Vita. Bivouac ledges break up the pitches on the lower wall.

current.area_walk_in: From the Longs Peak trailhead hike to Chasm Lake, then work around its north shore to the base of the East Face. The usual way up is the North Chimney, a loose fourth to low fifth class gully that leads to Broadway Ledge.
current.location: over on the Green Pillar's right-hand part

name: The Dragon
beta:
Nineteen pitches climb the left part of the wall, then six traversing pitches slant rightward and upward to the Dragon Chimneys, and five final pitches follow those chimneys out to the rim.

Pitch 25 is the crux, a descending traverse that finishes at the lip of a corner rated 5.11. Pack small-to-mid gear plus a few big pieces for the wide upper cracks, and consider two skinny ropes to tame drag on the traverses.
overview: The second route up the Painted Wall, a long line through the middle of the face that finishes in a set of loose chimneys bearing its name.

current.area_walk_in: Drop down the gully into the canyon, then head roughly a mile downriver along the water toward the talus fans below the wall.
current.location: Straight up the middle of the big face

name: The Fabulous Flying Carrs Route
beta: Five bolts lead to lowering anchors. If you want a tougher outing, avoid the corner down low and stay left of it.
overview: Pull through an overhang at the second bolt, then cruise jugs to a ledge with chains. Staying left of the corner low down keeps the grade honest.

current.area_walk_in: Continue east past the prominent descent gully beside Industrial Buttress; routes of note begin about 100 ft beyond the buttress's end, and the better lines lie further east.
current.descent: lower off
current.location: Five feet right of Pack O' Bobs, starting at a low first bolt on a slabby block

name: The Fixer
beta:
Smear up a steep friction slab beside the steep gully, climbing easy ground to a piton roughly forty feet up. Continue leftward, clipping several additional pitons while friction stays thin.

The top section is easy and unprotected, ending at a high alcove where the belay and rappel anchors sit beneath the headwall.
overview: Thin friction on a steep slab: easy ground to a first pin, then up and leftward on more pins, finishing on easy but unprotected rock at a high alcove.

current.descent: two ropes reach the ground; one rope gets you to Silver Spoon's gully belay
current.anchor: rap anchors in the alcove beneath the headwall
current.location: on the steep slab to the steep gully's right

name: The Ground Doesn't Lie
beta: A brief line tucked in a shallow alcove. Pull hard on steep rock with reasonable holds, passing three bolts, finishing at a hook-shaped opening plus a cold shut that was never welded.
overview: A short, steep three-bolt line in a shallow alcove with a tricky crux.

current.area_walk_in: Continue east past the prominent descent gully beside Industrial Buttress; routes of note begin about 100 ft beyond the buttress's end, and the better lines lie further east.
current.descent: lower off
current.location: Set back inside a shallow alcove

name: The Nose
beta:
Take the same opening as its neighbor, then leave that route after about fifty feet to jam the right flank of a detached pillar. Next, lieback a flake that faces right, step out left onto a broad crack, then belay from bolts.

Above, follow a crack out left to the margin of the enormous roof band, face climb up to a stance with big exposure, then work through the crux, a thin diagonal slash over a bulge, onto a slab. Finish via a groove and gentle ground up to the buttress summit.
overview: A classic, very exposed line straight up the rounded prow of Turnkorner Buttress, mixing a strenuous pillar crack, a layback flake and airy face climbing beside the huge ceilings.

current.area_walk_in: Walk the Black Canyon trail westward, passing under the entire west side of Lumpy Ridge, for two stiff miles. A little cairn flags the spur path, which winds up the steep forested hillside under the buttress and finishes close to an enormous flake propped against Turnkorner Buttress.
current.location: Directly beneath the nose, beside a large dihedral facing left, close to the buttress's lowest spot

name: The Spectacle
beta: Start from a flake that faces left and climb up and rightward past two bolts, where the hardest moves are, then stretch the rope to a third bolt, then belay beneath a chimney. The second pitch climbs the chimney into the gap behind the balanced-rock summit.
overview: A flake and bolted face on the rounded buttress below the lens, then a chimney up to the gap behind the top.

current.area_walk_in: Scramble up a groove-chimney under the left part of the lens, or retrace the descent gullies and traverse across to the trench beneath the route. Right Chimney is the wrong way in.
current.descent: descend a simple gully on the north, then walk round to the base
current.location: On the rounded buttress below the lens, starting up a flake that faces left

name: The Sting
beta: Walk around the dome's flank to the slab, then follow six quarter-inch bolts up it and stretch the rope over easy ground beyond two huge flakes. Extra medium cams help up there, and a 200 ft rope is the safest choice for this extended pitch.
overview: A long slab pitch on the dome that doubles as an ideal opening pitch for the famous crack above it. The line threads the rock separating a pair of dark water stains.

current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)
current.location: walk around the dome's west side to the foot of the slab beneath Scorpio Crack

name: The Yellow Traverse
beta: From the belay on the pedestal, descend a little leftward to a tiny ledge, then traverse upward and left under a dark groove, finishing at a belay beside a small tree.
overview: A committing leftward traverse beneath a dark groove on Wind Tower's south face, ending on a little-tree ledge; most parties continue up The Metamorphosis.

current.area_walk_in: Step across the plank footbridge spanning South Boulder Creek, then follow the path leading eastward beneath the south face.
current.descent: scramble northeast down ledgy slabs into a notch, rappel a short way on one rope from 2 bolts (or downclimb 5.4), then descend the gully west of the tower
current.location: From a stance on top of a pointed pedestal, reached by scrambling about 100 ft up a ramp that slants left, starting close to the tower's southeast edge

name: Theodore
beta:
The first pitch goes up a fine hand crack, the center one of three obvious cracks, ending on a terrace; the crack on its left makes an alternate start. Next, a crack at a gentler angle slants left to a stance beneath a jutting roof.

Simple cracks past a block lead to good ledges, and the last two pitches keep slanting left through gentle cracks and corners to the summit. A standard rack is all it needs.
overview: A pleasant moderate that takes four or five pitches of crack climbing on a slabby wall. Mostly it follows a middle crack, then drifts left up cracks and corners to the top.

current.area_walk_in: Follow the Summit trail until it runs along the base of the wall, then leave it and scramble uphill in the forest until you reach the face.
current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)
current.location: middle one of three distinct cracks at the base

name: Thindependence
beta: Two thin cracks run side by side up the wall; begin them from the crest of the leaning flake. Small gear down to a 1.5 cam and RPs is the rack.
overview: A short pitch of parallel thin cracks, handy as a last route of the day at the Book.

current.descent: Single-rope rappel from an anchor where the buttress drops off
current.location: Grassy ledge above the little cave by Pear Buttress, at its right end: twin fingertip cracks

name: Thinstone
beta: Follow the narrow crack in the open book up to the slot, taking RPs and cams up to a number 2.
overview: A thin-crack route that lines an open-book dihedral tucked behind the Tombstone, just beyond the corner from its neighbor Stretch Marks. It ends at the same slot that route uses.

current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)
current.location: Corner beside the arete behind the Tombstone, on its right, up a bushy gully around from Stretch Marks
